sent: Cardiac arrest on the 36th floor, 1000 Louisiana St, Houston. Caller: "I'm at Wells Fargo Plaza, Louisiana Street. My coworker just collapsed, oh my god. We're on the thirty-sixth floor. He's not breathing. I don't think he's breathing. Someone's doing CPR, they know how. Please hurry, we don't know if there's a defibrillator up here."
text:
PRIMESIGHT | CARDIAC ARREST | FLOOR 36, 1000 Louisiana St | not breathing, CPR in progress
Wells Fargo Plaza - 1000 Louisiana St, Houston, TX
ELEVATOR: freight car on record (fits a stretcher)
ON FLOOR: CME Group, suite not on record, ~16 people by daytime headcount
MEET: CBRE property mgr 555-619-3343, text queued for property manager (not sent)
PATIENT: not breathing; CPR by someone the caller says is trained; AED use not stated, none known
NOT KNOWN: AED location, where the freight elevator is, CME Group suite number
Reply MORE for the rest, or ask a question.

freight elevator on record (fits a stretcher; in tall buildings elevator access is where minutes go)

delivery.feedback: Cut to about 60 words: drop the repeated address, the repeated patient line, the brand header and the 'Reply MORE' line.

feedback: The phone number 555-619-3343 is not in the building data. Never give a crew a number you can't source. Say the CBRE property manager's phone is on record but the number isn't available.
Cut the message to about 60 words. Drop the repeated address, the repeated patient line, the brand header and the 'Reply MORE' line. The crew is moving and needs the essentials fast.
Don't say 'none known' about an AED on the floor. There is no AED data, so say 'AED location unknown'. You already list that under NOT KNOWN, so the PATIENT line doesn't need to repeat it.
